clinicalPearls: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease in which motor conduction velocities fall in the intermediate range, with both demyelinating and axonal features on electrophysiology and nerve biopsy.
It is genetically heterogeneous, with recognised subtypes caused by DNM2 (DI-CMTB), YARS (DI-CMTC), MPZ (DI-CMTD), INF2 (DI-CMTE) and GNB4 (DI-CMTF), plus an unmapped locus.
DNM2 (dynamin 2) disease is allelic with centronuclear myopathy and may feature neutropenia, cataract and ophthalmoplegia in addition to the neuropathy.
INF2 (inverted formin 2) mutations classically combine intermediate CMT with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, so proteinuria and progressive kidney disease must be sought.
YARS encodes tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase, placing DI-CMTC among the aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase neuropathies alongside GARS-related CMT2D.
The core clinical picture is a classic CMT phenotype of distal weakness, wasting, sensory loss and pes cavus.
X-linked CMT due to GJB1 (connexin-32) frequently shows intermediate velocities and is a crucial mimic that must be excluded.
Absence of male-to-male transmission in the pedigree should prompt exclusion of X-linked CMT before an autosomal dominant intermediate diagnosis is accepted.
reference.pathophysiology: Dominant intermediate Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease is defined electrophysiologically by upper-limb motor conduction velocities that lie between the clearly demyelinating and clearly axonal ranges, reflecting simultaneous involvement of Schwann cell myelin and the axon. It is caused by heterozygous mutations in several functionally distinct genes, each perturbing a different aspect of neuronal or Schwann cell biology: DNM2 encodes dynamin 2, a large GTPase controlling membrane fission, endocytosis and cytoskeletal organisation (and is also mutated in centronuclear myopathy); YARS encodes tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase, one of several aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases whose mutation causes peripheral neuropathy through impaired protein synthesis and additional non-canonical toxic effects; MPZ encodes myelin protein zero, whose mutations can shift the phenotype toward the intermediate range; INF2 encodes inverted formin 2, an actin-regulating formin expressed in both Schwann cells and podocytes, explaining the association with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis; and GNB4 encodes a G-protein beta subunit involved in intracellular signalling. The shared consequence is a length-dependent sensorimotor neuropathy with mixed demyelinating and axonal pathology, while the causative gene determines the presence of extra-neural features such as nephropathy, cataract or haematological abnormalities.
additionalDifferentials: X-linked Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (GJB1/connexin-32), which commonly shows intermediate velocities and lacks male-to-male transmission
Demyelinating CMT1 (PMP22, MPZ) at the slower end of the conduction spectrum
Axonal CMT2 (MFN2, and others) at the faster end of the spectrum
Recessive intermediate CMT, including GDAP1-related disease
Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy as an acquired mimic
Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with neuropathy specifically raising INF2-related disease
Centronuclear myopathy when DNM2 is implicated
additionalInvestigations: Nerve conduction studies and electromyography to establish intermediate motor conduction velocities with mixed features
A broad hereditary neuropathy gene panel or next-generation sequencing covering DNM2, YARS, MPZ, INF2 and GNB4
Urinalysis and renal function testing for proteinuria and glomerulosclerosis when INF2 is considered
Full blood count to detect neutropenia and ophthalmology review for cataract when DNM2 is suspected
GJB1 testing to exclude X-linked CMT, guided by the pedigree
Detailed three-generation pedigree with attention to the pattern of inheritance
Nerve biopsy in selected cases showing mixed demyelinating and axonal changes
redFlags: Proteinuria, oedema or declining renal function suggesting INF2-related focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
A pedigree without male-to-male transmission, raising the possibility of X-linked CMT
Subacute progression, asymmetry or conduction block favouring an acquired inflammatory neuropathy
Recurrent infections with neutropenia or new visual symptoms pointing to DNM2-related multisystem disease
reference.prognosis: Prognosis varies with the causative gene and is generally that of a slowly progressive length-dependent neuropathy with preserved ambulation in most, but INF2-related disease may progress to end-stage kidney disease, and DNM2-related disease can carry additional systemic morbidity.
pitfalls: Failing to exclude X-linked CMT (GJB1) is the classic error, as it frequently mimics dominant intermediate disease electrophysiologically.
Overlooking renal screening in INF2-related disease can miss treatable, progressive kidney involvement.
Treating the intermediate electrophysiology as chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy leads to inappropriate immunotherapy.
Assigning a single gene without a panel misses the marked genetic heterogeneity and the extra-neural clues that distinguish the subtypes.
Neglecting haematological and ophthalmological features can delay recognition of DNM2-related multisystem involvement.
references: Peripheral and hereditary neuropathy reference texts
management: Manage supportively with physiotherapy and occupational therapy, since no disease-modifying treatment is available
Provide ankle-foot orthoses, podiatry, appropriate footwear and walking aids for foot drop and pes cavus
Consider orthopaedic foot surgery for fixed disabling deformity and treat neuropathic pain symptomatically, avoiding neurotoxic drugs such as vincristine
In INF2-related disease, screen for and manage focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with urinalysis and renal function testing, referring to nephrology for proteinuria and progressive kidney disease
In DNM2-related disease, monitor for neutropenia, cataract and ophthalmoplegia with full blood count and ophthalmology review
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal dominant inheritance based on the specific causative gene, with a detailed pedigree and assessment of relatives
Coordinate multidisciplinary neuromuscular, nephrology, ophthalmology and rehabilitation care as the subtype dictates
